newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan says govt spending to rise 0.1 pct in 97/98.
newsitem.headline: Japan says govt spending to rise 0.1 pct in 97/98.

text.p: The government on Monday formally approved forecasts of major economic indicators for the fiscal year starting on April 1, including a real-term increase of 0.1 percent in government spending to 93.9 trillion yen.
Forecasts for other indicators including 1.9 percent real growth in gross domestic product (GDP) were unveiled last month. A special cabinet meeting on Monday approved the government's forecasts.

The figure for government spending for 1997/98, which includes spending by regional governments, represented a 1.1 percent nominal rise over estimated spending of 92.8 trillion yen in the current fiscal year.
Of the total, spending on public works projects was forecast to increase 0.5 percent in nominal terms to 43.6 trillion yen in 1997/98.
Government spending other than for public works is likely to total 50.3 trillion, up 1.6 percent from 1996/97.
The following are the official forecasts:
C/A surplus 6.9 trln yen 7.0 trln yen
Trade surplus 8.4 trln yen 8.4 trln yen
